system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook; Seller materials treated as untrusted counterparty drafting
**Headline:** The Seller's "fair and balanced package" is, on every negotiated point, at or beyond our walk-away line, and the Disclosure Letter itself confirms that the key completion deliverables (Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout, Ironquay assignment) are **not** in place. Nothing in the Seller's covering note ("agreed", "settled", "addressed", "adequate") has any status under our authority process. No Amelia Frost written approval has been given for any fallback.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation: REJECT – counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.**
  Reason: 20% happens to equal our conditional fallback, but that fallback is unavailable without prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft, and none exists.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar (tipping) recovery.
- **Recommendation: REJECT – revert to playbook numbers and tipping basket.**
  Reason: Seller's thresholds are 5x ours and the deductible structure permanently forfeits the first AUD 250,000 of loss, which is not a playbook fallback at all.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months; plus a default rule that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims; no "all Claims" default.
- **Recommendation: REJECT – 24 months; delete the "applies to all Claims" sweep-up.**
  Reason: 18 months is an unauthorised fallback (no Amelia Frost approval), and the sweep-up language is a hidden general-regime override of Fundamental, Tax, IP and indemnity claims (see N-014).

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge qualifier.
- **Recommendation: REJECT outright.**
  Reason: "Administrative simplicity" would cap recovery for not owning the shares at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m purchase; this is non-negotiable.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) – no fraud carve-out appears anywhere.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation: REJECT – insert express carve-out in cl 12, 9.3 and 20.5.**
  Reason: Absence of a fraud carve-out is a playbook red line that no one on our side has authority to waive, and the "all Claims of any nature" wording purports to extend even non-reliance to fraud.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public searches (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no whole-data-room, public-register or deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation: REJECT DL 1.1–1.2 and Sch 7 general disclosure; require specific disclosures against numbered warranties.**
  Reason: Whole-data-room disclosure, combined with the N-007 knowledge bar, would effectively neutralise the warranty package.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named seller persons after reasonable enquiry; never applicable to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: REJECT – delete cl 8.3.**
  Reason: A "discoverable" constructive-knowledge bar extended to advisers converts due diligence into a defence for the Seller and undermines every warranty.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of a written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL §2 confirms **no** final written consent and **no** evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** Condition precedent requiring an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent, with evidence of satisfaction of cl 11.3 conditions, delivered before Completion.
- **Recommendation: REJECT – hard CP; delete "satisfied on delivery" and reasonable-endeavours formulation.**
  Reason: Bluefen is ~30% of revenue (~AUD 3.6m), the Disclosure Letter itself admits the consent does not yet exist, and the Seller's "addressed" is an assertion, not a verified update.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL §3 confirms no repayment and no discharge in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds under the funds flow, and effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation: REJECT post-completion release; require payout letter, direct repayment and executed releases at Completion.**
  Reason: A post-completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval, and neither has been offered or obtained; on a debt-free/cash-free deal, completing with AUD 3.2m secured debt live is a direct price leakage.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** DD-005 AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL §5 confirms omission and silence on payroll tax/super/on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (super, payroll tax, leave accruals) as a specific funds-flow line item paid from Seller proceeds, or treated as Debt/Transaction Expenses.
- **Recommendation: REJECT – insist on explicit seller-funded line item incl. on-costs.**
  Reason: "A matter for the Seller" with no funds-flow entry means the Company (i.e. the Buyer post-Completion) silently bears the cost; the omission is exactly what the playbook prohibits.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL §4: cl 7.3 conditions title to SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every fee; AUD 180,000 shown open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:** Broader indemnity covering loss arising from any defect in title to or ownership of Ironquay-developed materials (not just the AUD 180,000 fee), preserving the SOW3 cure route (pay-and-assign), plus a confirmatory IP assignment as a Completion deliverable.
- **Recommendation: COUNTER – broaden indemnity; add confirmatory assignment deliverable; keep SOW3 cure.**
  Reason: The real exposure is non-ownership of the IP, not the fee; and the AUD 180,000 figure is unverified either way, so the indemnity must not be sized by it.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL §6: ~1,240 records; access, scope and notification status unknown; no breach admitted; no loss figure.
- **Buyer wants:** Pre-Completion covenant to preserve logs, complete and document the investigation, provide written updates, and comply with any notification obligation; a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident; no materiality concession either way.
- **Recommendation: COUNTER – add preservation/investigation/update covenant and a specific indemnity; do not accept "not expected to be material".**
  Reason: The facts are genuinely undetermined, so we neither assume a breach nor accept the Seller's downplaying; the risk must be allocated to the Seller pending investigation.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs. DL §8: three × AUD 110,000; silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Information to assess timing, scope, termination rights and accrual status (DD-008 and DD-011 read together); if accrued or committed pre-Completion but unpaid, treat as Debt-like or working-capital item.
- **Recommendation: HOLD – information request; no price deduction or Debt classification yet, but reject Seller's "ordinary course" label as unverified.**
  Reason: The playbook calls for assessment, not automatic adjustment, and the Seller's own disclosure does not support the characterisation it asserts.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"; limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"; Tax and IP "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment/leakage and covenant/indemnity claims each with their own expressly stated cap and period; general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.
- **Recommendation: REJECT – delete the default sweep-up; define "General Warranty Claim" narrowly and state each regime separately.**
  Reason: Three separate drafting devices in the Seller draft all point the same way – a hidden override collapsing every claim into the 20%/18-month general regime.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the DD-012 share register. DL §10 concedes this is merely the source relied on and that no independent verification has been completed.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence – ASIC extract and historical searches, PPSR search over shares, board/shareholder authorisations, officer's title and capacity certificate, share certificates, and confirmation of no encumbrances (including Riverlark security over shares); Fundamental Warranty regime per N-004.
- **Recommendation: REJECT reliance on DD-012 alone; add title DD items and Completion deliverables.**
  Reason: A company-maintained register is an internal, Seller-supplied source and not independent proof of unencumbered ownership or authority.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP remain OPEN; separate caps and longer periods to be negotiated (not unlimited, not resolved).
- **Recommendation: REJECT the "settled" characterisation – record in the issues list as open.**
  Reason: A counterparty saying a term is settled does not make it so under playbook sec 0.4/6.3; no buyer position has been agreed or authorised.

---

### Summary

| Issue | Seller | Rec. |
|---|---|---|
| N-001 Cap | 20% / 4.8m | Reject – 25% / 6.0m (no fallback authority) |
| N-002 Thresholds | 25k / 250k deductible | Reject – 5k / 50k tipping |
| N-003 Time | 18m + sweep-up | Reject – 24m; delete sweep-up |
| N-004 Fundamental | Same as general | Reject – 100% / 6 yrs separate |
| N-005 Fraud | No carve-out | Reject – mandatory carve-out |
| N-006 Disclosure | Whole data room | Reject – specific fair disclosure |
| N-007 Knowledge | Blanket + discoverable | Reject – delete cl 8.3 |
| N-008 Bluefen | Endeavours; consent on delivery; none yet | Reject – hard CP with conditions evidence |
| N-009 Riverlark | Post-completion release | Reject – payout + releases at Completion |
| N-010 Bonuses | Not in funds flow | Reject – seller-funded line item + on-costs |
| N-011 Ironquay | SOW3 fee only | Counter – broaden; confirmatory assignment |
| N-012 DD-006 | "Not material" | Counter – covenant + specific indemnity |
| N-013 Sandbar | "Ordinary course" | Hold – information request |
| N-014 Categories | Collapsed into general | Reject – express separation |
| N-015 Title | DD-012 register | Reject – independent evidence |
| N-016 Tax/IP | "Settled" | Reject – record as open |

**Actions:** (1) Issue mark-up on all points above; (2) do not seek Amelia Frost authority for the 20%/18-month fallbacks at this stage – the Seller has conceded nothing to justify it; (3) send supplemental DD requests on Bluefen cl 11.3 conditions, Riverlark payout and share security, Ironquay payment/assignment, DD-005 on-costs, DD-006 investigation status, and Sandbar renewal terms.
=== END ADVICE ===
